scope: Completed inspect-01/02/03 and comparison-01/02 with their original evidence, plus closed native-reader-01 addendum; later controller/homing runs excluded.
finding: Slow orientation drift remained against a stable camera scene in this fresh-boot record. RV05 changed 0.698 degrees in the baseline and 1.329 degrees in the comparison; Game08 changed 1.332 degrees in the comparison. The earlier large-drift episode was not reproduced, but this recording establishes neither a cure nor a motion-ready sensor.

application_staging.limitation: Successful native-Pi fake server and served UI verify staging only; no live ROS, motor, camera or provider behavior was exercised by this smoke check.

limitations: One fresh-boot record and observed scene stability do not explain or rule out the earlier large-drift failure.
Camera integer-pixel matches do not establish calibrated physical pose or exclude subpixel or between-frame motion.
Host receipt timestamps are not synchronized physical measurement times;07/02 nearest-receipt residuals are an offline comparison only.
Calibration-enable flags describe configuration, not calibration accuracy; feature restoration does not reverse background fusion evolution.
No robot motion, controller initialization, homing, policy or gain validation occurred in these sensor-only runs.

native_reader_addendum.interpretation: The same frozen native constructor/reset/parser also did not reproduce the prior severe-drift signature. Modest body yaw drift slowed during30s while the scene remained consistent at integer-pixel resolution. No-resetbaseline was already low-drift; this is not evidence that reset cured the fault. Reset, report enable order, native caching and elapsed time are not individually isolated. Neither sensor nor camera establishes motor readiness.
